verdict.summary: PayPal has two OAuth-style paths: Log in with PayPal, which only shares identity attributes and still needs a live review that PayPal says 'typically takes a few weeks', and seller onboarding through the Partner Referrals API, which grants permissions such as ADVANCED_TRANSACTIONS_SEARCH or INVOICE_READ_WRITE on a merchant's account but is 'available to approved partners only'. An agent that reads or acts on a user's PayPal transactions needs the partner path, so it depends on PayPal accepting your platform.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Sandbox apps are enabled as soon as you click Save, and PayPal says you can test multiparty flows in the sandbox before partner approval.

timeToProd.assumes: Partner approval to onboard users' merchant accounts with third-party permissions, which an agent reading transactions or invoices needs. Identity-only Log in with PayPal is faster: a few weeks of review.
timeToProd.waitingOn: A PayPal representative evaluating your platform after the 'Tell us about your platform' form, then live credentials and account-manager configuration (such as the return URL).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: PayPal publishes no partner approval timeline. The range is our estimate.

verdict.cost: No fee to apply is stated. Normal PayPal transaction fees apply to payments.

prerequisites.item: A PayPal account and developer dashboard access (sandbox accounts are created automatically)
prerequisites.why: Apps and credentials are created under Apps & Credentials, with separate sandbox and live apps.

prerequisites.item: A live privacy policy URL and user agreement URL
prerequisites.why: PayPal's privacy and security team reviews both before Log in with PayPal is activated for live.

prerequisites.item: Approved partner status (for acting on merchants' accounts)
prerequisites.why: The Partner Referrals endpoint 'is available to approved partners only'. You apply with the 'Tell us about your platform' form.

prerequisites.item: Users with PayPal business accounts in countries that can receive payments
prerequisites.why: Some onboarding paths need a business account, and sellers in send-only countries can't receive payments.

scopeTiers.impact: Gives name, email, address and verification status. No transaction data. Every scope needs approval before live; sandbox works on Save.

evidence.note: Scope strings from the live OpenID configuration.

scopeTiers.impact: Listed in scopes_supported but not documented on the current Log in with PayPal pages. Don't plan on them without confirming with PayPal.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Seen in the live discovery document; no current docs describe how to get them.

steps.title: Pick the path
steps.detail: Identity only → Log in with PayPal. Reading transactions, invoices or disputes, or acting on a merchant's account → partner seller onboarding via Partner Referrals.

steps.title: Create a sandbox app
steps.detail: Log in to the developer dashboard, open Apps & Credentials, create an app and copy the sandbox client ID and secret.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Dashboard URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20. We did not log in.

steps.title: Apply to become a partner
steps.detail: Submit the 'Tell us about your platform' form (company, website, solution description, company type, annual client volume).

steps.title: Draft the platform description and data-use justification
steps.detail: Write the solution description for the form, the list of third-party features you need and why, and privacy policy text covering AI processing of PayPal data.

steps.title: Build seller onboarding in sandbox
steps.detail: Call POST /v2/customer/partner-referrals with operations API_INTEGRATION and third-party features, redirect the seller to the action_url, and subscribe to MERCHANT.ONBOARDING.COMPLETED and MERCHANT.PARTNER-CONSENT.REVOKED webhooks.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: 'You must be an approved partner to use this integration' (s8). The operations value is from the schema.

steps.title: Wait for partner approval
steps.detail: A PayPal representative contacts you after evaluating your business needs.

steps.title: Configure live settings with your account manager
steps.detail: Get live credentials and work with your account manager to set the return URL for onboarding.

steps.title: Enable Log in with PayPal on the live app (optional)
steps.detail: Apps & Credentials > your live app > Other features > Log in with PayPal > Advanced Settings: return URL, attributes, privacy policy and user agreement URLs, then Save (this submits for review).

steps.title: Wait for Log in with PayPal review
steps.detail: PayPal's privacy and security team reviews; 'The review process typically takes a few weeks'.

agentCanDo: Choose between Log in with PayPal and partner onboarding
Draft the partner application text and feature justifications

Check the OpenID configuration and sandbox endpoints
humanMustDo: Log in to the developer dashboard and create apps
Submit the partner form and take calls with PayPal

blockers.symptom: Partner Referrals call fails in live with a permission or authorization error
blockers.cause: The endpoint is available to approved partners only.
blockers.fix: Apply via the 'Tell us about your platform' form and wait for approval; keep building in sandbox.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact live error string is not documented.

blockers.symptom: Log in with PayPal works in sandbox but not live
blockers.cause: Live apps are submitted for review on Save and aren't active until approved.
blockers.fix: Wait for review (a few weeks), with real privacy policy and user agreement URLs.

blockers.cause: Example URLs like https://example.com left in the privacy policy or user agreement fields.
blockers.fix: Replace them with live pages before saving the live app.

blockers.symptom: invalid_client / Client Authentication failed at the token endpoint
blockers.cause: Wrong client ID/secret, or sandbox credentials used against live (or vice versa).
blockers.fix: Use api-m.sandbox.paypal.com with sandbox credentials and api-m.paypal.com with live ones.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Seen on 2026-10-20 when calling the sandbox token endpoint with no credentials.

blockers.cause: The seller is in a send-only country, or hasn't confirmed their email.
blockers.fix: Check country support before onboarding and prompt sellers to confirm their email.

nuances.text: Log in with PayPal access tokens default to 28800 seconds (8 hours). The refresh token lifetime isn't stated.
Log in with PayPal uses pairwise subject identifiers, so the user ID differs per app.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: subject_types_supported: ["pairwise"] in the live discovery document.

nuances.text: Access to user attributes doesn't let you email users; you need a separate opt-in or opt-out for non-purchase communications.
Sellers can revoke partner consent at any time; MERCHANT.PARTNER-CONSENT.REVOKED tells you when.
The build-into-software onboarding option only includes cart capabilities, not Platform Fee, Delayed Disbursement, Partner Reporting or the Disputes API.
